question: A six year-old female presents for evaluation of dry skin, fatigue, sensitivity to cold and constipation. The patient’s mother recalls that the patient had surgery to remove a “benign mass” at the base of her tongue 3 months ago because of trouble swallowing. What was the likely cause of the surgically removed mass?

options.opd: Failed caudal migration of the thyroid gland
options.ope: Failed fusion of the palatine shelves with the nasal septum

analysis: The presentation of dry skin, fatigue, sensitivity to cold, and constipation in a six-year-old female is suggestive of hypothyroidism. The history of surgery to remove a mass at the base of the tongue, which was causing trouble swallowing, points towards a lingual thyroid. Lingual thyroid is a rare condition where the thyroid gland fails to descend from its embryonic origin in the base of the tongue to its normal pre-tracheal position in the neck. This failed caudal migration of the thyroid gland can lead to the formation of a mass at the base of the tongue.
